question.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{E}[X].$

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{ex}, & \frac{1}{e}<x<1 \\ \frac{1}{{x}^{2}}, & 1\le x<e\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the expected value using the following formula:

$$
\text{E}[X]={\int }_{S}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x
$$

 

We compute the expected value of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{{e}^{-1}}^{e}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{{e}^{-1}}^{1}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{e}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{{e}^{-1}}^{1}x\cdot \frac{1}{ex}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{e}x\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{{e}^{-1}}^{1}\frac{1}{e}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{x}{e}|}_{{e}^{-1}}^{1}+\operatorname{ln}⁡x{|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{1}{e}-\frac{1}{{e}^{2}}+1-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{e}-\frac{1}{{e}^{2}}+1\end{aligned}
$$
